headline: PM Tarique Rahman begins daylong tour of Kishoreganj for development programs
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman embarked on a daylong visit to Kishoreganj to participate in various development initiatives, including family card distribution and tree planting. The district is abuzz with preparations for his first visit since taking office.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman departed Dhaka for Kishoreganj on Sunday, August 16, for a daylong tour. He is traveling by road to participate in various development and welfare programs across the district.

During his visit, the Prime Minister will cover the district headquarters and three upazilas. His agenda includes distributing family cards, planting trees, releasing fish fry, and inaugurating the Fisheries Week.

He is also scheduled to present grants and honorariums to various individuals and institutions. Extensive preparations are underway in Kishoreganj for his arrival, marking his first visit to the district since assuming office.
Following a full day of engagements, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will conclude his programs and return to Dhaka from Kishoreganj in the evening.

headline: Presidential election nominations scrutinized Sunday, only 349 MPs to vote
summary: Bangladesh is set to hold its presidential election this week, but only 349 Members of Parliament will have the opportunity to cast their votes. Nominations will be scrutinized on Sunday.
details: Bangladesh is preparing for its presidential election this week, a unique process where only 349 Members of Parliament are eligible to vote. This contrasts sharply with general elections, where the entire adult population participates.
The scrutiny of nominations for the presidential candidates is scheduled for Sunday. This step will finalize the list of contenders for the nation's highest office.
The limited electorate for this special election has sparked public discussion. Many are questioning the implications and public sentiment surrounding such a restricted voting process.
caption:
Only 349 Members of Parliament will vote in Bangladesh's presidential election this week. Nominations are set for scrutiny on Sunday.

Bangladesh is preparing for its presidential election this week, a unique process where only 349 Members of Parliament are eligible to vote. This contrasts sharply with general elections, where the entire adult population participates.

The scrutiny of nominations for the presidential candidates is scheduled for Sunday. This step will finalize the list of contenders for the nation's highest office.

The limited electorate for this special election has sparked public discussion. Many are questioning the implications and public sentiment surrounding such a restricted voting process.
